transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. I guess I'm here because of my eating. What really made me make the appointment is that... well, once I start eating sometimes, it feels like I hit some sort of switch. I just keep going and going. Even while part of me is sitting there thinking, you know, Dennis, just stop already, I just can't seem to actually stop.
After these episodes of eating, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. I've never tried throwing up or taking laxatives or anything like that. And I'm definitely not working out a bunch either. I just... I don't know, I just kind of sit there feeling really full. I don't do anything to try and undo it.
How do you feel emotionally after these episodes of overeating?

Honestly, I feel pretty embarrassed. I just get kind of grossed out with myself. It really bothers me because I'm usually pretty disciplined when it comes to my classes and my robotics stuff. So when I eat like that... it just makes me feel like I'm completely not in control.
Do you find that you tend to eat these large amounts of food even when you aren't actually feeling physically hungry?

I don't really think so. I mean, usually when I start eating, I actually am hungry... like, it's a normal time for a meal or I just got out of class and need a snack. It's just that once I start, I end up eating way past the point where I'm full. But I haven't really noticed myself starting to eat all that food when I'm not physically hungry to begin with.
On average, how many times a week would you say these episodes of eating past the point of fullness occur?

I'd say it happens most weeks, usually at least one night a week. Sometimes it's two nights, especially if I have a lot of deadlines or if there's just a bunch of food sitting around the apartment. It's been happening like this since early in the semester, so... probably for the last three or four months, it's been a pretty steady pattern.
During these episodes, do you find that you are eating much more rapidly than you would during a normal meal?

Yeah, I definitely do. During those times, I eat really fast. Usually, I'll just be, like, standing at my desk between doing homework and playing a game, and I just kind of inhale it. I barely even taste what I'm eating, honestly. It's like... I just realize afterward that all the food is gone in just a few minutes.
During these episodes where you eat rapidly and feel out of control, do you tend to eat by yourself because you feel embarrassed about how much you are eating?

Yeah, I do. If my roommates are hanging out in the kitchen or the living room, I'll just eat a normal-ish amount while I'm out there. But then... I'll usually grab extra stuff and take it back to my room later. I just don't want them seeing how much I'm actually eating, you know? It's definitely something I hide.
How much does the fact that these episodes happen impact your overall mood or how you feel about yourself on a daily basis?

It definitely impacts me. Afterward, I just feel embarrassed and... kind of grossed out with myself. It's frustrating because I'm usually pretty disciplined, you know, with my schoolwork and my robotics team. So when this happens, it just makes me feel like I'm completely not in control of myself.
Does the distress you feel after these episodes persist or affect your day-to-day life beyond just the immediate feeling of embarrassment?

Well, it hasn't really stopped me from doing what I need to do. I still make it to my classes and go to robotics practice and everything. But... I do notice it the next day. I'll feel kind of sluggish in the morning, or I'll be sitting in class just feeling distracted, worrying if my roommates noticed what I was doing the night before. So, I guess it bothers me a lot mentally, but it hasn't completely knocked me off track or stopped me from functioning, if that makes sense.
